questions.scenario: A transfer fails with `DataIntegrityViolationException`; further down the trace is `Caused by: PSQLException: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "journal_reference_key"`.
questions.question: What is the most useful reading of this trace?
options: The top line is always the root cause, so the problem is in Spring
Spring has a bug in its exception translation
The database is down
The root cause is a repeated journal reference hitting a unique constraint; find the first frame in your own package to see which call inserted it
questions.explanation: The last Caused by is usually the root cause; your own first frame shows where your code was involved.

questions.scenario: A loop processes 20,000 transfers and fails only for reference TRF-2026-0193.
questions.question: How do you stop the debugger exactly there?
options: A conditional breakpoint with `t.reference().equals("TRF-2026-0193")`
Step over 20,000 times
Add Thread.sleep before the loop
Restart the IDE in safe mode
questions.explanation: Conditional breakpoints suspend only when the expression is true.

questions.scenario: A service catches an exception somewhere deep in a library and returns null, so the error never reaches your logs.
questions.question: Which debugger feature finds where it is thrown?
options: Evaluate Expression
A watch on a local variable
Drop Frame
An exception breakpoint on that exception type
questions.explanation: Exception breakpoints stop where the exception is thrown, even if it is later caught.

questions.scenario: Requests time out every afternoon. CPU is low. Three thread dumps taken ten seconds apart show most `http-nio` threads parked in `HikariPool.getConnection`.
questions.question: What does this indicate?
options: Garbage collection is too frequent
The JVM has run out of heap
The database connection pool is exhausted; find what holds connections for long (slow queries, long transactions, leaks) rather than only enlarging the pool
A deadlock between two HTTP threads
questions.explanation: Threads waiting in getConnection mean connections aren't being returned fast enough.

questions.scenario: Heap use grows after every full GC until the service fails with `OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space`.
questions.question: What is the best next step?
options: Capture a heap dump (or enable HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError) and inspect the dominator tree for what retains the memory
Switch to a different garbage collector
Double the heap and close the ticket
Restart the service every night
questions.explanation: Growing post-GC heap suggests a leak; the dominator tree shows which references keep objects alive.

questions.scenario: Which logging practices make production problems easier to solve? (Choose two.)
questions.question: Select two.
options: Putting a correlation id in the MDC for each request and returning it to the client
Logging full request bodies including card numbers
Logging with parameters and passing the exception as the last argument
Catching exceptions and logging only e.getMessage()
questions.explanation: Correlation ids link a request's lines; parameterised logs with the exception keep the stack trace. Sensitive data must never be logged.

questions.scenario: A teammate wants to enable JDWP remote debugging on the production server to investigate a bug quickly.
questions.question: What is the right response?
options: Allow it and disable the firewall temporarily
Allow it during business hours only
Allow it if the port is changed from 5005
Refuse: an open debug port allows arbitrary code execution; reproduce locally, or use logs, metrics and dumps
questions.explanation: Remote debugging is for local or isolated environments; production needs safe diagnostics.
